evals.prompt: Set up Cyclone UI in my pnpm React/Tamagui app and add the Button component under src/components/ui. Show me how to render it with the dark theme.
evals.expected_output: Installs the CLI in the app, initializes the selected path, previews and adds button, installs dependencies and Cyclone tokens/state, wires the theme provider and renders Button using its real API.
expectations: Previews button before adding it and runs pnpm install afterward
Shows Button.Text inside the copied Button component
Does not claim to have installed into an unspecified app

evals.prompt: Our Next.js app already has components.json and a locally edited button. Add the current registry button without losing our edits, and keep its client directives.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the existing config and local changes, previews or diffs the registry version, preserves or merges edits instead of forcing init or overwrite, and explains the RSC directive setting.
expectations: Inspects the existing components.json instead of rerunning init with force
Uses the registry already configured in the app unless the user supplies an override
Uses a read-only preview or diff before any write
Explains how to merge or preserve local edits without blind overwrite
Correctly describes rsc true or omitted as preserving registry client directives
Does not claim to have changed the unspecified app

evals.prompt: Add the Cyclone UI dialog to a workspace that uses a custom registry URL and npm. Tell me what files and packages the command changed.
evals.expected_output: Adapts commands to npm, respects the specified registry, discovers and previews dialog and its dependencies, then reports copied files, package changes, and checks performed.
expectations: Uses npm commands or explicitly adapts to the npm package manager
Uses the workspace custom registry rather than silently replacing it with the public default
Previews dialog before installation and accounts for internal component dependencies
Does not invent specific changed files or packages without seeing the target workspace or registry
Explains how to inspect components.json and package.json changes after installation
